scope: Official Web player RAF-owned asynchronous fixed-step update/accept/draw scheduling; no gameplay changes or completion-counter inflation

prior_browser_evidence.interpretation: The unchanged completion counter exposes actual repeated snapshot submissions followed by skipped snapshot numbers. Source inspection identifies independent timer simulation and RAF drawing as a phase-aliasing path; simulation and submitted-frame advances near 60 do not imply 60 distinct submissions.

implementation.clock: RAF timestamps, fixed 1000/60 ms simulation steps
implementation.boundary: Await bounded sequential tick transactions, then draw once before scheduling the next RAF
implementation.backpressure: One update transaction at a time, including worker requests; no independent simulation timer or separate free-running completion-driven draw loop
implementation.catch_up: At most 5 steps per draw; excess whole steps counted as dropped; fractional remainder retained
implementation.rounded_timestamps: Early step tolerance min(0.25 ms,stepMs/100), approximately 0.167 ms at 60 Hz; negative accumulator debt retained rather than discarded
implementation.visibility: Hidden time excluded; generation changes suppress old asynchronous draws/catch-up tails; paused UI redraws remain allowed
implementation.counter_contract: Unchanged: accepted simulation publications, completed world/UI/cursor submissions and changed submitted frame numbers stay separate

validation.command: node --test web/shared/async-scheduler.test.mjs web/shared/player-completion.test.mjs web/shared/player-profile-main.test.mjs web/shared/player-profile-main-backend.test.mjs web/shared/startup-player-entry.test.mjs web/shared/ordered-physical-player-entry.test.mjs web/shared/player-pointer.test.mjs
validation.historical_disposition: Concurrent save-publication import initially required the extracted-main VM fixtures to import the actual serializedSavePayload helper; the final run includes that fixture update
cases: 600 rounded 60 Hz RAF timestamps submit each advanced snapshot exactly once without dropped steps
Actual player tick/accept/draw plus real worker backend: 120 RAF transactions, 120 tick commands, 120 changed snapshot submissions, drop 0
Pending actual worker response schedules no additional tick and claims no stale completed draw
High-refresh zero-step redraws and low-refresh multiple-step draws keep distinct presentation counts honest
Long-stall catch-up is bounded and fractional time is retained
Pause, visibility transitions, stop/restart and reset during asynchronous work suppress stale draws and hidden-time catch-up
Update/render errors stop scheduling and report once
Existing readiness, incomplete-world/UI/cursor and read-only completion metrics regressions remain passing

independent_review.scope: Read-only final async-scheduler.mjs: stop/start during an in-flight tick, generation invalidation, finally scheduling, sequential catch-up/drop bounds, high-refresh redraws and retained rounding debt
independent_review.execution: Reviewer ran no tests or builds

native_pixel_snap_gate.toolchain: Rust 1.95.0 GNU; pinned RUSTC, task-local CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME, w64devkit PATH and self-contained LIBRARY_PATH; normal debug profile
native_pixel_snap_gate.evidence: Tool execution transcript; no separate raw log captured
native_pixel_snap_gate.contract: Nested inline pixel_snap=true fails with UI_HOST_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED before asset/GPU preparation; false retains existing admission; native capability descriptor reports unsupported with the official Web host required

limits: These controlled scheduling tests are correctness evidence, not an actual browser FPS benchmark or GPU scanout proof
Combined update/draw CPU work still has to fit the display budget; catch-up under overload intentionally reduces distinct presentations
No JYRogue game files, gameplay rules, renderer replacement or reported completion-counter definitions were changed
